newsitem.title: USA: GM, Chrysler report lower February U.S. car sales.
newsitem.headline: GM, Chrysler report lower February U.S. car sales.

text.p: General Motors Corp. and Chrysler Corp. Monday reported lower domestic car and truck sales for February, reflecting tough competition from Japanese automakers and a cooler market than a year ago.

GM, which continued to suffer from low availability of several key new car models, said February sales totalled 356,124 vehicles, down 7.1 percent on daily selling rate basis, with car sales down 9.3 percent and truck sales off 4 percent.
There were 24 selling days last month compared with 25 in February 1996.
"It is not a bad market," Chrysler President Robert Lutz said of current U.S. industry conditions. "It has just deflated a bit from a great market."
Speaking to Reuters at the Geneva auto show in Switzerland, Lutz added that the U.S. market looks "fairly stagnant," while other markets around the world appear to be backsliding.

Chrysler said its U.S. sales for the month totalled 198,983 cars and trucks, 2.8 percent below sales in February 1996, which set a record. Chrysler car sales fell 6.1 percent while light truck sales edged down 0.3 percent.

Honda Motor Co. Ltd., benefiting from the dollar's strength against the yen, reported a 9 percent jump in February U.S. sales to 66,289 units, with most of the gains coming in imported cars and trucks.
Nissan Motor Co. Ltd. reported a 15.5 percent increase for its Nissan and Infiniti brands to 63,913 units, with import car sales up 38.1 percent.
"It's not booming, but it's holding in there at a healthy state," J.P. Morgan analyst David Bradley said of the February sales results.

Some analysts estimated that February's seasonally adjusted annual sales rate could reach 15.4 million units, down from 15.7 million units a year earlier. Severe winter storms in January 1996 pushed significant vehicle deliveries into February, making it the strongest sales month of 1996.
At Chrysler's Auburn Hills, Mich., headquarters, Chrysler Executive Vice President James Holden said he was encouraged by the company's February performance.

"Coupled with the accelerating traffic we saw at dealerships as the month progressed, that tells us the spring selling season may be at full throttle for Chrysler in March," Holden said in a statement.
GM officials also tried to put a positive spin on their company's sales decline.

Of the 43,259-unit decline in GM sales, about 35,000 units were from cars that GM has discontinued in the past year -- the Chevrolet Caprice, Corsica and Beretta, the Buick Roadmaster, the Oldsmobile Ciera and 98, and the Cadillac Fleetwood.
New GM car models being launched this year are not yet available in significant numbers to make up the difference, said GM spokesman Dean Rotondo.
However, while GM sold as many as half of the discontinued cars to rental fleets, the new products are gaining a bigger share of the more profitable retail market, Rotondo said.
About 77 percent of all Pontiac Grand Prix mid-size cars, for example, are being sold to retail customers.
"We really gained three pounds of muscle and lost five pounds of fat when we look at what's happening to the mix of sales," Rotondo said.

J.P. Morgan's Bradley said GM fared better than he expected, but added that the automaker cannot continue to use the production launches as an excuse for lower sales. "They've been using it for several months now. Sooner or later they need to show positive sales results," he said.

Ronald Zarrella, GM vice president of marketing and sales, said he was encouraged by dealer orders for nearly 34,000 Chevrolet Malibus, adding that 90 percent of them were for retail sales. GM sold 5,822 Malibus in February, compared with 3,586 in January.
But sales dimmed for GM's much-touted new EV1 electric car, falling to 24 units in February from 70 in January.
GM attributed its truck sales decline to shortages of full-size sport utility vehicles and extended cab pickup trucks.
GM's stock rose $1.375 to $59.25 on the New York Stock Exchange. Chrysler shares fell 37.5 cents to $33.625.
Ford Motor Co. is expected to report sales on Tuesday. Ford shares rose 25 cents to $33.125.
